props.name: activated carbon removes COS and iron carbonyl at room temperature
props.statement: Passing the make-up gas through activated carbon removes catalyst poisons such as carbon oxysulfide and iron carbonyl at room temperature; this requires injecting about 0.5 g ammonia per m3 and oxygen slightly above the stoichiometric amount for oxidizing the sulfur.

props.name: low bromine number indicates good raw methanol
props.statement: According to the operators the bromine number of the raw methanol should be as low as possible; a high number indicates unsaturated alcohols and ketones; the upper limit is 5 to 7, good product 3 and excellent 1.

props.name: catalyst life 6 months to 1 year; spent charge largely pulverized
props.statement: The normal catalyst life is said to be 6 months to 1 year; about 60–70% of a spent charge is found pulverized, and the catalyst is changed when the converter pressure drop reaches about 20 atm.

props.name: converter inlet CO must be below 20% to avoid higher alcohols
props.statement: Plant experience indicates that the CO content of the gas entering the converters must be less than 20% to prevent formation of appreciable quantities of higher alcohols.

props.name: constant converter pressure drop is important
props.statement: It is very important to maintain a constant pressure drop across the converter, since a sudden variation of even a few atmospheres increases the undesirable components of the raw methanol; as the catalyst ages the pressure drop is increased very gradually with the circulator by-pass valve to maintain production.

props.name: dimethyl ether forms as an undesirable side reaction

evidence.note: OCR of 2 CH3OH -> (CH3)2O + H2O; quote withheld: sha256:2402033f1fb79cb76ff2e139ee485dfe0f190b3626dc95278caf4f8a04d43324 chars:102

props.statement: An undesirable side reaction giving small amounts of dimethyl ether also takes place (2 CH3OH → (CH3)2O + H2O).

props.name: graphite must be added below 30 °C
props.statement: In the new Oppau method, the temperature must not exceed 30 °C when graphite is added, otherwise lumps are formed; the method has not yet been used on a large scale.

props.name: modern plants use a different catalyst and about 3 times the space velocity of isobutyl synthesis
props.statement: According to interrogated personnel, the modern methanol plants built elsewhere by I.G. are very similar to the new isobutyl plant at Oppau, but a different catalyst is used and the space velocity for methanol synthesis is about 3 times that for isobutyl synthesis.

props.name: chromic oxide must be added rapidly (thixotropic mixture)
props.statement: According to Leuna, the chromic oxide must be added very rapidly because the zinc chromate mixture is thixotropic and a non-homogeneous product may result, giving a poor-quality catalyst.

props.name: Oppau process generally similar to that used in the United States
props.statement: In general the Oppau methanol synthesis process is similar to that used in the United States, but certain process and design features and improvements in newer German plants are of particular interest.
